content: Azithromycin, marketed as ZITHROMAX for injection, contains the active ingredient azithromycin, which is classified as an azalide, a subclass of macrolide antibiotics. It is intended for intravenous administration. The chemical name of azithromycin is (2R,3S,4R,5R,8R,10R,11R,12S,13S,14R)-13-[2-ethyl-3,4,10-trihydroxy-3,5,6,8,10,12,14-hepta-methyl-11-oxy]-1-oxa-6-azacyclopentadecan-15-one. Azithromycin is a derivative of erythromycin, but it differs structurally by the incorporation of a methyl-substituted nitrogen atom into the lactone ring. ZITHROMAX for injection is composed of azithromycin dihydrate as the active ingredient, along with the inactive ingredients citric acid and sodium hydroxide. The product is supplied in a lyophilized form within a 10-mL vial, which is equivalent to 500 mg of azithromycin for intravenous administration. When reconstituted according to the instructions on the label, the preparation yields approximately 5 mL of ZITHROMAX solution for intravenous injection. Each milliliter of the reconstituted solution contains azithromycin dihydrate equivalent to 100 mg of azithromycin.
